facts.statement: The only known specimen of Orthogenysuchus is a skull without lower jaws, cataloged as AMNH 5178.
facts.quote: The holotype, known as AMNH 5178, is the only known specimen belonging to the genus and consists of a skull lacking the lower jaws.

facts.statement: Fossils of Orthogenysuchus were found in the Wasatch Beds of the Willwood Formation in Wyoming, dating to the early Eocene.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from the Wasatch Beds of the Willwood Formation of Wyoming, deposited during the early Eocene.

facts.statement: While later publications placed Orthogenysuchus in Crocodylidae, recent analyses suggest it might be a pristichampsid or a synonym of Pristichampsus.
facts.quote: Later publications assigned the genus to the Crocodylidae, but more recent analyses propose that it is a pristichampsid or even a synonym of Pristichampsus.

facts.statement: A 1999 study placed Orthogenysuchus in a new clade that also included the Miocene caimanines Purussaurus and Mourasuchus.
facts.quote: In 1999, Orthogenysuchus was placed within a new clade containing the Miocene caimanines Purussaurus and Mourasuchus.

facts.statement: Orthogenysuchus predates Purussaurus and Mourasuchus by approximately 30 million years, implying significant ghost lineages for those groups.
facts.quote: Orthogenysuchus antedates these genera by around 30 million years, suggesting that they both had significant ghost lineages.

facts.statement: The proposed clade linking Orthogenysuchus and Mourasuchus remains informally described because it relies on ambiguous characters due to the poor preservation of the holotype.
facts.quote: However, the clade is based primarily on ambiguous characters as a result of the poor preservation of the holotype of Orthogenysuchus, thus has not yet been formally described.

facts.statement: Orthogenysuchus shares with Mourasuchus a long, broad snout, extremely wide external nares, and many small maxillary alveoli.
facts.quote: Orthogenysuchus shares with Mourasuchus a characteristically long, broad snout, extremely wide external nares consisting of the nasal aperture and dorsal fossa, and many small maxillary alveoli.

facts.statement: Orthogenysuchus lived during the Ypresian stage, between 56 and 51.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Ypresian (56 to 51.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: Orthogenysuchus is classified within the subfamily Caimaninae.
The genus Orthogenysuchus was named by Mook in 1926.
The holotype, known as AMNH 5178, is the only known specimen of the genus and consists of a skull without the lower jaw.

facts.statement: In 1999, Orthogenysuchus was placed within a new clade grouping the Miocene caimanines Purussaurus and Mourasuchus.
facts.quote: En 1999, Orthogenysuchus fue situado dentro de un nuevo clado que agruparía a los caimaninos del Mioceno Purussaurus y Mourasuchus.

facts.statement: Orthogenysuchus predates these genera by nearly 30 million years, suggesting the existence of a significant ghost lineage.
facts.quote: Orthogenysuchus antecede a estos géneros por cerca de 30 millones de años, lo que sugiere que existiría allí un significativo linaje fantasma.

facts.statement: However, the clade is based primarily on ambiguous characters due to the poor preservation of the Orthogenysuchus holotype, so it has not been formally described.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, el clado está basado primariamente en características ambiguas como resultado de la pobre preservación del holotipo de Orthogenysuchus, y por lo tanto este no ha sido descrito formalmente.

facts.statement: Orthogenysuchus shares with Mourasuchus a long and wide snout, extremely wide external nares, and many small maxillary alveoli.
facts.quote: Orthogenysuchus comparte con Mourasuchus un hocico largo y ancho, narinas externas extremadamente amplias consistentes en la abertura nasal y la fosa dorsal, y mucho alvéolos maxilares pequeños.

facts.statement: The presence of Orthogenysuchus in North America during the Eocene suggests a dispersal event of caimans from South America after the original spread of early alligatorines and caimanines in South America at the Cretaceous-Tertiary boundary.
facts.quote: La presencia de Orthogenys en Norteamérica durante el Eoceno sugiere que hubo un evento de dispersión de los caimanes desde Suramérica después de la propagación original de los primeros aligatorinos y caimaninos en Suramérica que ocurrió en el límite entre el Cretácico y el Terciario.
